picks.title: Erdős #124: Aristotle's Lean proof settled a weaker formal statement, not the BEGL96 problem
picks.claim: Aristotle (Harmonic), run by Boris Alexeev, produced a Lean proof of the Formal Conjectures statement erdos_124, publicised as solving Erdős Problem #124.

inputs.desc: Original Lean challenge statement (commit 61e0260, 2025-11-12) with '= 1' where the docstring says '>= 1'
Forum thread with Alexeev's Aristotle proof and the scope discussion

picks.error: The formal statement was weaker than intended (typo '= 1' for '>= 1', and the erdosproblems wording omitted BEGL96 hypotheses), so the checked proof does not settle the BEGL96 conjecture.

confirmation.quote: Aristotle solved 'a' version of this problem ... but not 'the' version.

picks.confirmed_by: Independent party and maintainers: Thomas Bloom (erdosproblems.com), Boris Alexeev; Formal Conjectures maintainer mo271 merged fix PR #1307 for issue #1306

computational_claim: A Lean computer-checked proof claimed to settle Erdős #124.
replayable_inputs: Lean statement pinned by commit in a public repo; proof posted publicly.
error_confirmed_primary: Issue #1306 and fix PR #1307 by maintainers; Bloom's forum summary.

picks.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V2: showcased Putnam 'proofs' accepted only through a Lean apply? synthetic-sorry bug
picks.claim: DeepSeek-Prover-V2's technical report (first release, 2025-04-30) presented Lean 4 proofs of PutnamBench problems (e.g. putnam_2005_a4, putnam_2007_b4) as machine-verified solutions.

inputs.desc: Tech report at the first commit; Appendix B shows the proof
Minimal reproduction of the apply? synthetic-sorry bug, with the Lean version
Ammanamanchi-Bhat-Biderman (ICML 2026), Appendix D: full buggy proofs of putnam_2005_a4 and putnam_2007_b4 (Lean 4.9.0)

picks.error: The proofs contain apply? steps that leave a synthetic sorry; with a universe-level elaboration error the theorem is silently never added to the environment, so Lean reported success without kernel verification.

confirmation.quote: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 produced an obviously wrong proof of a Putnam problem

picks.confirmed_by: Independent party (issue by hanwenzhu, closed by Lean maintainer kim-em via fix PR #8231) and the ICML 2026 audit by Ammanamanchi, Bhat and Biderman

computational_claim: Claimed machine-checked Lean proofs of benchmark theorems.
replayable_inputs: Proof text is public (report at pinned commit; full text in the ICML paper) and the Lean version is stated.
error_confirmed_primary: Lean issue accepted and fixed by maintainers; peer-reviewed audit reproduces it.

picks.title: Erdős #7 (Erdős-Selfridge odd covering): AI-assisted 'sorry-free' Lean proof rests on a provably false axiom
picks.claim: A May 2026 AI-assisted (Aristotle) Lean 4/Mathlib development claimed a sorry-free proof of the Erdős-Selfridge odd covering conjecture, modulo three axioms said to encode BBMST (2019) results.

inputs.desc: Original upload (commit 0edac82, 2026-05-02) with ErdosSelfridge_v11.lean; later commits replace files
Forum thread with the claim, the refutation and the author's acknowledgement

picks.error: The axiom bbmst_sf_lt_one asserts sieveProd(...) < 1, but sieveProd as defined is a product of factors 1 + x/s > 1, so the axiom is false (a mistranslation omitting BBMST's c_0 factor).

confirmation.quote: My formalization omitted c_0 entirely, making the axiom provably false.

picks.confirmed_by: Author (jinooklee) acknowledging an independent party's refutation (Nat Sothanaphan); Thomas Bloom then restricted the thread to axiom-free Lean proofs

computational_claim: A Lean-checked proof claim (sorry-free, with custom axioms).
replayable_inputs: Lean source pinned at a public commit; the axiom's falsity is checkable by evaluating/proving sieveProd >= 1.
error_confirmed_primary: Author's public acknowledgement on the erdosproblems forum.

picks.title: bbchallenge (2022): backward-reasoning decider ignored tape writes; 1,253,418 'decided' BB(5) machines reverted
picks.claim: The Busy Beaver Challenge's backward-reasoning decider (Feb 2022) declared 1,253,418 machines of the 5-state seed database non-halting.

inputs.desc: Decider source at the buggy commit c4a4596 (2022-02-09)
Index of undecided machines, created when the results were cancelled
Machine #55897188 used in the bug report; the seed database is public

picks.error: The decider ignored the symbol written on each transition, which can produce false positives and false negatives, so its decisions were unsound and were cancelled.

confirmation.quote: However you example proves me wrong.

picks.confirmed_by: Maintainer (tcosmo, bbchallenge) acknowledging the report by milomg/atticuscull; fixed via PR #5

computational_claim: A decider's classification of over a million Turing machines as non-halting.
replayable_inputs: Seed database and decider source at a pinned commit are public.
error_confirmed_primary: Maintainer acknowledged the bug and cancelled all the decider's results.

picks.title: Löbbing-Wegener (1996): wrong BDD count of closed knight's tours on the 8x8 board
picks.claim: Löbbing and Wegener computed with binary decision diagrams that the number of (undirected closed) knight's tours on an 8x8 board is 33,439,123,484,294.

inputs.desc: EJC 3 (1996) R5 paper giving the method; input is the 8x8 knight graph, fully specified
OEIS entry for undirected closed knight's tours on 2n x 2n boards (8x8 value 13267364410532)

picks.error: The published count is wrong (it is not divisible by 4 as symmetry requires); the correct count, computed independently by McKay, is 13,267,364,410,532.

confirmation.quote: The number of knight's tours given in the paper is incorrect

picks.confirmed_by: Authors (Löbbing and Wegener comment, 1996-05-15) and independent party (B. D. McKay comment, 1997-02-18)

computational_claim: An exact count produced by a BDD computation.
replayable_inputs: The input (8x8 knight graph, closed undirected tours) is exact and public; counting can be re-run by BDD/ZDD or McKay's method.
error_confirmed_primary: Authors' own comment on the journal page plus McKay's independent recount.

picks.title: Mathematica 8-9.0.1 returns wrong (and non-repeatable) determinants of explicit 14x14 big-integer matrices
picks.claim: Mathematica's Det, used by Durán, Pérez and Varona to test conjectures on Casorati determinants of orthogonal polynomials, returned stated exact determinant values for explicit 14x14 integer matrices.

inputs.desc: Durán-Pérez-Varona, 'The misfortunes of a trio of mathematicians using computer algebra systems. Can we trust in them?' (Notices AMS 61(10), 2014): full explicit matrices and the wrong outputs

picks.error: The determinants Mathematica returned were wrong, and differed between evaluations of the same matrix; exact recomputation (e.g. in PARI, Sage, Maple) gives a different value.

confirmation.quote: It does appear there is a serious mistake on the determinant operation

picks.confirmed_by: Authors and the software vendor (Wolfram Technical Support reply quoted in the paper); bug fixed in Mathematica 10.0.2
picks.date_confirmed: 2013-12-11 (arXiv v1, which quotes Wolfram's reply); Notices AMS 2014-11

computational_claim: An exact integer determinant computed by a CAS.
replayable_inputs: The exact matrices are printed in the paper; exact determinants are cheap to recompute.
error_confirmed_primary: Peer-published by the authors, with vendor acknowledgement and a later fix.

alternates.reason: Distinct ATP input-encoding class, seconds to replay, author-acknowledged; ranked below F06 because the original claim was hedged.
Cleanest independent refutation and trivial replay; same wrong-count class as F03.
Certified (DRAT) refutation of search counts; heavier replay and the 1989 program is lost.

selection_notes: Six error classes, one each: formal statement weaker than the claimed problem (F01); checker defect that accepted claimed AI proofs (F10); Lean proof resting on a provably false axiom (F06); unsound decider behind a large classification (F14); wrong exhaustive count (F03); wrong exact result from a trusted CAS (F05). Each has public pinned inputs and an author, maintainer or vendor acknowledgement, not only a third-party claim. Three are AI-assisted (2025-2026), three are not (1996-2022). None comes from openai/math: its 2026-10-07 withdrawals and fixes concern informal, unformalized arguments and fail criteria 1-2. F11 (unrefereed, unacknowledged) and F12 (likely a deliberate exploit) were left out on confirmation strength.
